source_cards.title: FFT-Based Dynamic Range Compression
source_cards.bounded_summary: A feed-forward time-frequency DRC computes energy, gain targets and smoothed gain independently per time-frequency cell. It supports high-resolution multiband compression and frequency-dependent sidechain ducking, but introduces many controls, latency and computational cost. The examples are demonstrations, not perceptual validation.
limitations: No formal listening test establishes preference or transparency.
Example parameters were intentionally aggressive for spectrogram visibility.
Latency, temporal resolution and reconstruction artifacts are not reduced to a single quality metric.
The paper is not a rock-specific evaluation.
The companion implementation was not executed in this run.

source_cards.title: Parametric Resynthesis of Measured Spatial Room Impulse Responses
source_cards.bounded_summary: The abstract separates early-reflection resynthesis via Herglotz analysis from late reverberation via a directional feedback-delay network and reports matching spatial correlation and Energy Decay Relief against measured SRIRs.
unknown_until_deep_review: failure cases and applicability to stereo rock ambience

knowledge_cards.title: Time-frequency DRC is a two-dimensional control system
knowledge_cards.claim: A spectral compressor is defined by its time-frequency analysis and reconstruction as well as by threshold, ratio and ballistics.

knowledge_cards.title: Spectral floor is an artifact guardrail
knowledge_cards.claim: A lower bound on per-band gain is required to prevent harsh attenuation; useful bounds must be chosen by controlled listening rather than copied from an illustration.

knowledge_cards.title: Resolution settings are method context, not presets
knowledge_cards.claim: FFT length, hop, band count and sample-rate choices determine temporal and spectral behavior and cannot be transferred as genre defaults.

knowledge_cards.title: Gain-map visibility is not preference evidence
knowledge_cards.claim: An intentionally visible spectrogram change demonstrates controllability, not better punch, transparency or musical preference.

knowledge_cards.title: Free multitrack access does not imply AI-training rights
knowledge_cards.claim: A catalogue may permit educational mixing while separately prohibiting AI training or automated dataset use without contributor-specific permission.

rule_candidates.title: Expose spectral DRC analysis and reconstruction
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: Evaluating any time-frequency or spectral compression candidate.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Log FFT/filterbank, window, hop, sample rate, band mapping, latency, reconstruction and per-band gain trace.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Impulse and sweep measurements plus loudness-matched full-mix and mono listening.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: The implementation cannot expose these variables or audible artifacts cannot be separated from desired gain action.

rule_candidates.title: Bound per-band attenuation experimentally
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A spectral branch can create narrow or deep gain holes.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Test a project grid of 0/1/2/3 dB maximum per-band attenuation with identical detector intent; do not copy paper demonstration values.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Gain-map inspection, spectral-hole audit and blind loudness-matched listening.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: A smaller bound performs equally well or tone becomes hollow, unstable or processed.

rule_candidates.title: Separate gain-map fit from artifact and preference outcomes
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: Comparing full-band, crossover-multiband and FFT-based dynamics.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Report desired gain action, latency/artifacts and Dmitry's blind preference independently.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Matched controls, objective traces and randomized loudness-matched A/B.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Only the optimized or visualized gain map improves while artifacts or preference worsen.

rule_candidates.title: Enforce source-specific audio rights
rule_candidates.when_to_apply: A free multitrack is considered for automated evaluation, dataset ingestion or model training.
rule_candidates.what_to_change: Record track-level rights and obtain contributor-specific permission before any automated or training use; otherwise restrict to manual listening.
rule_candidates.how_to_verify: Retain the applicable terms and permission record beside the Reference Card.
rule_candidates.cancel_when: Rights are ambiguous or permission does not cover the intended use.

experiment_plans.title: Full-band versus crossover and FFT frequency-dependent ducking
controls: matched detector intent and maximum action where feasible
experiment_plans.success: The smallest-complexity branch improves the intended collision without audible holes, smear or image change.
experiment_plans.cancel: Desired action is not matched, artifacts appear, image destabilizes or blind preference does not beat unchanged.

experiment_plans.title: Spectral attenuation-floor grid
experiment_plans.cancel: A lower bound performs equally well or a higher bound sounds hollow or unstable.

experiment_plans.title: FFT temporal-resolution audit
experiment_plans.cancel: Longer resolution smears events or shorter resolution creates unstable frequency action.

experiment_plans.title: Parallel drum return blend after transcript validation
experiment_plans.prerequisite: obtain permitted content for at least one queued authoritative video or use an independently documented processor setup
experiment_plans.cancel: Density comes mainly from level increase, bleed/noise becomes intrusive or attacks flatten.

novelty.summary: The 2017 FFT-DRC paper was absent and is now fully read; the 2026 SRIR paper is newly discovered but remains abstract-only. The multitrack card records a concrete AI-training restriction. Four current papers were removed as duplicates.
novelty.publication_vs_discovery: The FFT paper was published in 2017 and discovered for this project on 2026-09-16; the SRIR paper is a 2026 DAFx publication discovered the same day.

safety: All rules remain candidate with auto_apply:false.
No audio, DSP engine, repository code, runtime configuration or active rule changed.
No user or commercial audio was downloaded, extracted or uploaded.
No numeric DSP metrics were invented.
No paid subscription, GPU job or arbitrary third-party Space was used.
handoff: Do not treat FFT compression as multiband compression with more bands. Expose analysis and reconstruction parameters, preserve an unchanged baseline, and judge gain-map fit, artifacts and preference separately. Cambridge multitracks require contributor-specific permission for AI training or automated dataset use.
